Subject: Re: Rate card questions: prompt/prefix cache billing (technical note)

Throwing in the tech details so you have language to share. TL;DR: billing aligns to compute performed and tokens delivered; cache hits avoid model compute and are billed at a small retrieval rate. Details below — feel free to paste into procurement language.

1) Exact prefix cache hit (full cached response)
   - No model compute occurs on our serving runtime; we do not run the model kernel.
   - You are billed for the response payload (output tokens) at a "retrieval" price that is lower than the standard per-token model compute price. Retrieval price is expressed as a percentage of the standard output token price (we typically use 10% for hosted customers unless otherwise negotiated).
   - Input tokens that were used to find the cache key are not billed as model compute; they are accounted for in our request processing but not charged as full model-token compute on a cache hit.

2) Partial cache hit or cache-then-model (stitching)
   - If the cache returns a prefix that we can reuse and we only run the model for the remainder, we bill:
       * Retrieval fee for cached portion (10% of output token rate by default)
       * Full compute charge for any tokens produced by running the model on the non-cached suffix (standard per-token model rate)
   - In telemetry we tag these as "cache_partial" and surface the breakdown in the Console (cache bytes, compute tokens).

3) Cache miss
   - Full model run: you are charged standard input + output token rates (same as an uncached request).

4) Determinism/temperature and TTL
   - We only guarantee cached hits for deterministic settings (fixed temperature & sampling). If requests differ in sampling params, they are treated as misses. TTLs are configurable; long TTLs increase hit rate but may serve stale responses if your prompt context changes.

5) Example estimate (very rough)
   - Baseline traffic: 100M response tokens/month; expected hit rate 70% with prefix-cache.
   - With 10% retrieval fee on hit tokens: billed tokens equivalent = 0.7 * 100M * 0.10 + 0.3 * 100M * 1.0 = 37M token-equivalents billed at compute price 
   - That corresponds to ~63% reduction in compute-billed tokens vs no cache.

6) Observability
   - Console shows cache_hit_rate, cache_partial_rate, billed_compute_tokens, retrieval_tokens; we can add the fields to your dashboards for the trial.

Attachment: prefix_cache_pricing_notes.md (text/markdown)

If you want I can draft a one-paragraph procurement-friendly description and a sample line item for the PO.

—Dev

Olivia — quick update. Dev confirmed the billing semantics (see below). I drafted a concise procurement-friendly paragraph and a commercial concession we can offer FitCommerce to simplify the PO. Please review and tell me if this will work for procurement.

- Procurement text (single paragraph to paste into PO):
  "Redwood Inference offers a prefix-cache feature. When a request is served entirely from cache (exact prefix match under deterministic settings), there is no model compute; the customer is billed a cache retrieval fee equal to 10% of Redwood's published per-output-token rate for hosted API usage. Partial cache hits are billed with a retrieval fee for the cached portion and full compute charges for the model-run portion. Cache misses are billed at standard input+output token rates. Retrieval fee and rates will be listed on the invoice and aggregated under 'Compute — Retrieval'."

- Commercial concession: FitCommerce commits to a 6-month baseline (monthly committed spend $XX,XXX) and Redwood will apply a 12% committed discount to the standard hosted API token rates for the term. The retrieval fee remains 10% unless otherwise negotiated.

If that looks good I will send a formal quote and attach the rate card. I flagged Marissa for approval of the concession — Marissa, can you confirm we can offer 12% for 6 months for this account?

—Karthik

Hi Olivia / FitCommerce procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal confirmation, here is a short, procurement-ready summary you can put in the PO plus the commercial terms we discussed: 

1) Billing summary (paste-able language):
   "Redwood Inference prefix-cache behavior:
    - Full cache hit: no model compute; billed at a retrieval fee equal to 10% of Redwood's published per-output-token rate for hosted API usage. Input tokens used only for cache key lookup are not billed at model compute rates for cache hits.
    - Partial cache hit: cached portion billed at retrieval fee; generated suffix billed at standard per-token compute rates.
    - Cache miss: full model run billed at standard input+output token rates.
    Retrieval fees and billed compute will appear as separate line items on the invoice."

2) Commercial terms:
   - 6-month committed baseline: $28,000/month (est).
   - Committed discount: 12% off standard hosted API token rates for the 6-month term.
   - Retrieval fee for cached responses: 10% of published per-output-token rate (unchanged).

3) Next steps:
   - If procurement is happy with the PO language above, we will generate a formal quote and include the rate card and a short attachment that maps example traffic to expected billed compute (we can include a 3-month projection).
   - We will enable console dashboards for cache_hit_rate and billed_compute_tokens for the account during onboarding.
